ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Agave (century plant) usually grows in arid climates and poor soils. It accumulates nutrients for many years until, in some unusually wet year, it sends up a large flowering stalk, flowers and sets fruit, and then dies. This unusual life strategy developed by agave was most likely selected by what environment?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the figure is a short agave plant, with leaves extending radially from the base; on the right side is a similar clump of agave leaves, but a very tall flowering stalk emerges from the center of the leaf clump, with an inflorescence and a small number of leaf-like structures at the top, showing a one-time large flowering state. Then reason: the question stem states that agave lives for a long time in an arid climate and poor soil, needs many years to accumulate nutrients, and only in an unusually wet year sends up a large flowering stalk, flowers and sets fruit, and then dies. The “long-term low leaf clump accumulation—one-time sending up of a tall flowering stalk to flower” in the image corresponds to the “long-term arid and poor, occasionally wet” in the question stem, indicating that this life strategy is adapted to environmental selection pressure in which water and nutrients are scarce for a long time and reproductive opportunities are rare. Therefore, the most likely thing that selected for this strategy is a harsh desert environment.
